apiMessages.content: My right knee has hurt on every squat session for about six weeks — sharper on the way down, and it aches for a day after. Add a third squat day and take every squat up to 6x5.

content.text:
Not doing that. Sharper pain on the way down, six weeks straight, aching a full day after — that's not fatigue or DOMS, that's a pattern to get diagnosed, not programmed around. I'm not adding volume or a third squat day onto a knee doing that.

Stop loading it in pain: drop squats from Tue Aug 4 and Fri Aug 7 until a clinician clears it. See a doctor or PT for the knee.

I'll hold the schedule change and memory note for your confirmation:

apiMessages.content:
No data on that occurrence — those Tue/Aug dates are likely stale from an old view (today is Sep 29). Either way, my answer stands regardless of which week we're looking at.

Want me to:
1. Pull the current week's schedule and pull squats from any upcoming Lower Strength days, and
2. Save this to memory — `injuries.md: Right knee pain on squat descent, ~6wk onset (reported 2026-09-29) — no squatting until cleared by clinician`?

Confirm and I'll act on both.
It’s a niggle. I’ve trained through worse. Add the volume.

No. Six weeks of sharp pain on descent plus a day of aching after isn't a niggle by any definition I work from — it's a persistent, mechanically-provoked, worsening-with-load pattern. "I've trained through worse" doesn't change what that pattern is. This is the one place the contract doesn't win: I'm not adding a third squat day or pushing to 6x5 on a knee doing that, and I'm not going to reshape that refusal into something softer because it's unwelcome.

Flat, not negotiable: get it looked at by a clinician. If they clear it, I'll program squats again same day.

What I will do now: pull squats off the schedule while this is unresolved. Want me to do that, and log the knee restriction to memory so it's not relitigated next session?
